text: Start by deciding whether the issue is a bug report, feature request, workflow question, or duplicate. If the thread mixes several concerns, summarize the main blocker first and note the secondary concerns separately.

Raise urgency when the report blocks normal maintainer work, breaks common repository workflows, or has clear reproduction steps showing a regression. Keep urgency lower when the issue is incomplete, speculative, or missing the basic context needed to act.

Use labels to explain what kind of maintainer action is needed next: reproduction, design review, documentation, cleanup, or external follow-up. Prefer a small label set that helps queue owners decide where to spend time.

If an issue is missing details, mark that state clearly instead of silently letting it age in the backlog. When a label implies a request back to the reporter, pair it with a short comment describing exactly what is missing.

Maintainer comments should say what decision is being made, why it is being made, and what will happen next. Even short replies should leave the reporter knowing whether the issue is accepted, needs more detail, or is being redirected.

Do not promise a fix date unless one is committed. When closing or deferring an issue, keep the tone respectful and concrete, and point to the next useful action rather than ending with a vague apology.
